content.title: About
content.content: Greens, canned, cooked is a blend of chopped leafy vegetables such as spinach, kale, broccoli and green peas that have been heat‑treated and sealed in airtight cans. The product is ready to eat without further cooking, retains most of its nutrients, and has a tender texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canned greens are often used in military rations and backpacking meals because of their long shelf life.
The "Greens" blend typically includes at least five different leafy vegetables, increasing the variety of vitamins and minerals.
Thermal processing destroys most microorganisms, allowing storage for up to three years at room temperature.
Canned vegetables are frequently fortified with a small amount of salt and antioxidants to preserve color and flavor.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Leafy greens provide B6, folate (B9) and riboflavin (B2), which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K supports blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Carotenoids and polyphenols protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from leafy vegetables promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Vegetables are low in calories, making them a good choice for weight management.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned greens often contain added salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Vegetable allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to specific leafy vegetables.

items.title: BPA in packaging
items.content: Metal cans can have trace amounts of BPA; choose BPA‑free labeled products if this is a concern.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Greens can be eaten straight from the can, added to salads, soups, pasta, or omelets. They may be gently warmed in the microwave or on the stove, but this is optional.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the contents in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 3‑5 days.
